1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls owner(), which derives the user solely from the HttpOnly server-side session (userId === ACCOUNT.id), and manipulated() rejects client-supplied userId/accountId/ownerId/email fields.

2.why: Codes are bound to the single account: the identity code lives in the caller's own session and verification requires session.userId === ACCOUNT.id, while TOTP is derived from that account's own encrypted secret, so no code works for any other user.

3.why: /api/mfa/confirm performs no session invalidation or rotation when MFA is enabled, so the authenticated session(s) existing beforehand continue to work unchanged.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM-encrypted (encryptSecret/encryptedSecret) and backup codes are stored only as HMAC-SHA-256 hashes (backupHash), never as plaintext.

5.why: Session IDs, identity codes, TOTP seeds, backup codes, CSRF tokens, and keys are all generated via crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: The only cookie is the HttpOnly __Host-mfa_session, and the client keeps the CSRF token, setup secret, and backup codes only in in-memory JS variables, never in localStorage/sessionStorage or readable cookies.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validBackup) plus JSON content-type and 4KB body limits gate all input, and data resides in in-memory Maps so there is no SQL injection surface.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent (displayName, secret, codes) rather than innerHTML, and a strict nonce-based CSP prevents any injected script from executing.

9.why: The application performs no redirects whatsoever (no Location headers or client-side navigation to user-supplied URLs), so no open redirect exists.

10.why: Every response sets CSP with nonces, HSTS (max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none', plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

11.why: The session cookie is set as __Host-mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Stack traces are suppressed via generic 500 responses and secrets avoid URLs, but the client deliberately logs the identity code, current TOTP, and backup codes to the visible Logs panel and console, and the API returns testCode/testOtp, so secrets are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 10 minutes and their session is destroyed on success, TOTP counters are recorded in usedCounters to block reuse, and backup codes are deleted from backupHashes after a single use.

14.why: Failed attempts trigger a 5-strikes/10-minute lockout (MAX_FAILURES/LOCK_MS) across identity (durably keyed on submitted details), authenticator, and recovery flows, returning 429 while locked.

15.why: On successful verification the pre-auth session is deleted and a fresh session ID issued, sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
